answer: A reserve-attestation ledger can flag any identity whose claimed balances show a negative delta against on-chain inflows, forcing each agent to prove control of a cold-wallet key before transacting. At dawn each epoch, the exchange reconciles hot-wallet outflows to cold-wallet signatures, so a sybil must fund every fake identity with real, traceable capital rather than a minted credential. That reconciliation cost scales linearly with each fabricated orchard of identities, though a wealthy attacker can still absorb it if verification stays purely financial.
